text:
jake_sales: SensCare legal signed off; they want a 48h POC next Tue. They have a VPC that peers to their colo via VPN. Question: fastest path to reach our Private API for their smoke tests — VPCE (Privatelink) or VPC peering to our transit VPC? Also asked for a short test API key for curl.

mina_se: VPCE is usually fastest and least invasive. Since they already have a VPN to a VPC, they can place the interface endpoint in that VPC and traffic will flow over the VPN to that VPC -> VPCE. DNS is the main gotcha.

omar_infra: Notes from infra side:
- VPCE: need subnets in 2 AZs, SG on endpoint allowing inbound TLS from their app CIDR, private-dns enabled. No route table edits required for endpoint traffic.
- Peering: requires non-overlapping CIDRs, create+accept pcx, update RTs both sides. Peering is heavier ops.

ryan_devops: Quick VPCE CLI we give to customers to run in their account:
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0f1e2d3c \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-abc123 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb \
  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c3 \
  --private-dns-enabled
```
Test: `dig +short private-api.redwood-inference.internal` -> should return ENI IPs. If not, check private-dns and resolver path.

elaine_sec: Security policy: we cannot provide org-wide long-lived keys for POCs. Options we offer:
- Ephemeral bearer token (816h) scoped to the POC org and rate-limited (preferred)
- Short-lived API key rotated daily (only if ephemeral token is incompatible)
Also ask whether their colo inspects TLS or terminates TLS on the appliance; if so, cert pinning or mTLS may be required. mTLS support is available but requires additional setup time.

jake_sales: They asked specifically: "If VPCE is used and their resolver is on-prem, will DNS resolve automatically?"

mina_se: If their on-prem DNS is authoritative and not forwarding to AWS resolver, it will not resolve automatically. Recommend one of:
- Configure their DNS to forward the redwood domain to the VPC resolver used by the VPN
- Add split-horizon records in their DNS (temporary for POC)
- Use /etc/hosts in the POC pods/hosts as a quick workaround

omar_infra: Peering caveat: if they pick peering through transit, ensure we exchange return routes and their NAT rules allow the ephemeral ports. Also NACLs need to permit the traffic.

runbook_bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc-privatelink-vs-peering (includes SG templates, route table examples, and DNS troubleshooting).

jake_sales: Action items:
1) ryan_devops: prepare ephemeral token flow + README and sample curl (today)
2) mina_se/omar_infra: deliver a trimmed VPCE + SG snippet and note on DNS forwarding for their network team (ASAP)
3) elaine_sec: one-page security checklist and question on TLS inspection/mTLS requirement (today)
4) I will schedule kickoff once they confirm which VPC will host the endpoint (tomorrow AM)

mina_se: I'll drop the curl example here when the token flow is ready. Keep this thread as the single place for handshake.
